title: Explicitly compute all rubric metrics before reporting results
when_to_use: When task instructions specify multiple output metrics that will be scored against a rubric.
experience:
- Review the scoring rubric or task requirements to extract a comprehensive list of required metrics.
- Before generating final insights, compute all required metrics in a structured table (e.g., open rate, click-through rate, orders per 1k, GMV per 1k).
- Verify the presence and accuracy of each metric for every analysis dimension (e.g., segment, time window, variant).
- If a metric cannot be computed due to data constraints, document the limitation and propose an acceptable proxy.
- Use computed metric tables as the sole source for deriving recommendations and conclusions.
checklist: Compute all metrics for all segments
Validate metric values against known anchors
Explicitly flag missing metrics before concluding
common_failure_prevented: Failing to report required metrics (e.g., CTOR, orders per 1k, GMV per 1k) despite having the data, resulting in low rubric scores.

title: Define explicit anchor thresholds for segmentation decisions
when_to_use: When segmentation requires grouping continuous variables (e.g., high/low volume, send frequency, audience size).
experience:
- Identify any continuous variable mentioned in the task that requires categorical grouping (e.g., 'high send window', 'scale stratification').
- Determine appropriate anchor points (e.g., median, quartiles, top/bottom 10%) based on data distribution and business logic.
- Create a clear parameter table defining each segment's threshold and label.
- Compute sample sizes and performance metrics for each defined segment.
- In the final report, explicitly state the thresholds used and justify them.
common_failure_prevented: Skipping explicit segmentation (e.g., 'high send day') or using arbitrary/implicit thresholds, which violates rubric requirements.

title: Integrate all required data sources for multi-table analysis
when_to_use: When the analysis depends on combining multiple tables to compute required metrics.
experience:
- Map each required metric in the task to the specific column(s) and table(s) needed to compute it.
- Design a join strategy (e.g., key-based, time-based, aggregation) to combine tables at the appropriate grain.
- Validate join quality (e.g., match rate, nulls) before proceeding with analysis.
- If direct joins are impossible, explicitly propose and implement an acceptable approximation (e.g., campaign-level proxy for user-level retention).
- Document any data limitations and their impact on result validity.
checklist: Map metrics to source tables and columns
common_failure_prevented: Using incomplete data (e.g., ignoring the persons table) leading to missing critical metrics like retention rates.
